enonce_markdown: The climate of the southern part of Cameroon (the South, Centre, East and Littoral Regions) is:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Cameroon stretches from near the equator northwards, so its climate changes from south to north.

### Solution

The south, close to the equator, is hot and wet nearly all the year: it has an **equatorial** climate. A Mediterranean climate has dry hot summers, a desert climate has almost no rain and a temperate climate has cold winters; none of these is found in the south of Cameroon.

**Answer: b.**

enonce_markdown: Which Region of Cameroon has one long dry season and only one rainy season in the year?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The further north, the longer the dry season; the tropical (Sudan) type has a single rainy season.

### Solution

The Far North Region, in the north of the country, has the tropical (Sudan, grading into Sahelian) climate with one short rainy season and a long dry season. The South, East and Centre Regions have the equatorial type, with rain in most months.

**Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown: State TWO differences between the climate of the south of Cameroon and the climate of the north. Name ONE type of natural vegetation found in each zone.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare the same elements (rainfall, seasons, temperature range, vegetation) for the two zones.

### Solution

| Element | South (equatorial) | North (tropical / Sudan) |
|---|---|---|
| Rainfall | Heavy, in most months | Less, in one season only |
| Seasons | Short dry seasons (two rainy and two dry seasons) | One rainy season and a long dry season |
| Temperature range | Small | Larger, with very hot days in the dry season |

**Vegetation:** the south has the equatorial rain forest; the north has savanna (tall grass with scattered trees, becoming shorter grass and thorny shrubs towards Lake Chad).

enonce_markdown: Bamenda in the Western Highlands is cooler than Douala on the coast, although both are in the same country. The main reason is that Bamenda:
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Temperature falls as height above sea level increases (about 6.5 degrees Celsius for every 1000 m).

### Solution

Bamenda lies on a high plateau, so the air is cooler because of **altitude**. It is not nearer the equator than Douala in any significant way, and it is not closer to the sea. It does not have a desert climate.

**Answer: d.**

choix.texte: is at a much higher altitude

enonce_markdown:
The monthly rainfall (in mm) at two stations in Cameroon, A and B, is given below.

| Month | J | F | M | A | M | J | J | A | S | O | N | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Station A (mm) | 5 | 20 | 120 | 180 | 210 | 150 | 100 | 130 | 230 | 260 | 90 | 10 |
| Station B (mm) | 0 | 0 | 5 | 30 | 90 | 150 | 220 | 280 | 180 | 40 | 0 | 0 |

Which station is more likely to be in the north of Cameroon, and why?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Read the pattern of the months: count the rainy peaks and the dry months, and compare it with the climatic type.

### Solution

Station B has one rainy season (about June to September, with a peak of 280 mm in August) and five months with almost no rain (November to March); this is the tropical pattern of the north. Station A has rain in every month, with two peaks (May and October) and a total of 1505 mm: this is the equatorial pattern of the south. The yearly total of B (995 mm) is lower than that of A, so the last option is wrong.

**Answer: a.**

choix.texte: B, because it has one rainy season and several months without rain
A, because it has rain in every month
A, because it has two rainy seasons
B, because it has the higher yearly total

enonce_markdown: Explain how the climate of the north and the climate of the south of Cameroon influence the choice of crops grown there. Use ONE crop example for each zone.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Link the temperature and rainfall of each zone to the needs of the crop, and say why the crop does badly in the other zone.

### Solution

**North (tropical, with a long dry season): cotton** (or millet and sorghum). Cotton needs a rainy season for growth, followed by a long dry sunny period for the bolls to open and be picked without being spoilt by rain.

**South (equatorial, hot and wet all the year): cocoa** (or oil palm, banana or plantain). Cocoa trees need heat, a high and regular rainfall and shade, which the equatorial zone provides; in the north the long dry season would make them wither.
